newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dow rolls through 8,000 barrier.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dow rolls through 8,000 barrier.

text.p: Ho hum, or so it would seem for the Dow Jones Industrial Average, which Wednesday strolled through the 8,000 milestone.
Just five months after clearing the 7,000 level, the Dow has again defied bear cries of "overvalued" and "overbought" and surpassed another millennium marker.

Analysts are quick to point to the fact that each 1,000 points becomes easier on a simple percentage basis but just as many acknowledge that with each hurdle passed, the market receives a powerful psychological boost.

"We're still transfixed by these numbers and round numbers especially make us nuts," said Ralph Acampora, director of technical research at Prudential Securities. Acampora has already forecast a 10,000 reading on the Dow in 1998.
The blue chip average's latest 1,000 point march fell short of the standard set in February, when it completed a four-month sprint from 6,000 to 7,000 and left many on Wall Street breathless.
"Back in February, people were saying 'My God, 7,000,'" said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
Now, as then, Bleier argued that the lofty numbers alone were not reason enough to quit the market.
"Eventually, something is going to shake the tree," Bleier said, "but until the tree gets shaken, you stay with the primary trend and that remains a powerful uptrend."
The Dow's gains today also capped a whirlwind run that doubled the blue chip average in less than 2-1/2 years.
In contrast, it took the Dow more than 14 years to climb from 1,000 to 2,000 and another eight years before it first cleared the 4,000 level on February 23, 1995.

Since then, the ascent has been dizzying. Nine months later, on November 21, the Dow pierced 5,000 for the first time, closing at 5023.54. It needed 11 more months to pass 6,000 on October 14, 1996 and then blew through 7,000 a mere four months later.
"There's no question it's accelerating, and that's an indication of more to come," Acampora said.
"I've talked to institutional investors and it's like they're frozen in the headlights," he said. "Is there a little bit of panic in the buying? Sure, there is."
In fairness, the Dow had its results "juiced" a bit in March, when it cast out some underperformers, replacing Bethlehem Steel Corp, Woolworth Corp, Texaco Inc and Westinghouse Electric Corp.

In their places, now stand Johnson & Johnson, Wal-Mart Stores Inc, Travelers Group Inc and Hewlett-Packard Co. Hewlett-Packard has proved to be a particularly potent addition of late, ranking as the strongest Dow component in each of the last three sessions.

Fine-tuning aside, though, the mystique builds each time a major marker falls. With so much ground already covered, it is perhaps inevitable that the market's eyes are already fixing on the future five-digit Dow.
"The ultimate milestone is now Dow 10,000," Bleier said. "We're living in a time with very strong demographics for the market and this blows away everything that has come before."
